utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we begin, as usual, by taking the appearances for today, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. I'm Tom Hannis, with Gramsci Di Fazio and Crispian Smith for the Prosecution. I have one scheduling matter I'd like to raise before we call in the witness, once the Defence have made their notices.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Ms. Tatjana Savic appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Igor Pantelic for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I actually have two scheduling matters, and one of them is regarding next witness, ST-168. He arrived yesterday afternoon. I've only had about 45 minutes with him. The Defence has requested to interview him, and we presently have time available at 10.30 and 11.30 this morning for them to meet with him. So my request is when we finish with the current witness that we recess for the day and start with ST-168 tomorrow. I'm scheduled for two hours of direct. The Defence I think has four and a half hours total, but I'm told it will probably be less. At any rate, we feel confident that even if we don't start with him until tomorrow morning we will finish with him on Friday. And I understand the Defence has no objection to that request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Hannis. We were alerted to this last evening. So when the present witness has been released, we will take the adjournment to tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Now the second matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The second matter relates to the first witness next week, ST-130. We're presently scheduled to sit in the morning; we would like to request that we sit in the afternoon. I understand that there is a courtroom available. And if the parties and the Court has no objection, that would be our request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We would have the Registry look into it, and we will discuss it and get back to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Would this be on Monday?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, the Registry has confirmed that it is possible to do it, and the Judges have no objection. So we would sit on Monday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Kezunovic. Before we resume, I remind you you're still on your oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I start, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Kezunovic.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: We will now resume. And before I ask you one specific question, I want to give you an example. All political parties - I don't mean only the victorious ones, but all of them - and state authorities, the municipality, the Executive Board, administrative agencies, and other organs from municipality level to republic level, were often in a position dealing with certain affairs to engage one or more experts, connoisseurs of certain areas, to help them out in deciding on a stance, making a feasibility study, an analysis, an expert report, et cetera; for that purpose, they frequently established expert commissions and asked such commissions to provide an expert report or an analysis. Are you familiar with this practice?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But right now, I could not think of any specific examples, although perhaps the best example is the preparation for that analysis of data derived from the census that was conducted in Bosnia in April 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, we lost the e-court altogether. The LiveNote and the e-court and everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I understand we will have it back in about five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, I'll give you an illustration to make things easier. Every municipality has its own statute, that is, the basic document, a small-scale constitution on municipality level that governs the fundamentals of the operation of this community. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: That enactment is passed by the Municipal Assembly, but in order to endorse it, somebody, an expert, must prepare a draft. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: That's when a so-called statutory commission is established, including prominent lawyers, usually prosecutors or judges, or perhaps university professors, if the municipality is lucky to have them. They prepare a draft document which is then forwarded for deliberation.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But as an executive authority at local level --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Cvijetic, unless I'm missing something, could you tell me where we're going with this excursion into administrative law?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just stated an example, and I will move right away to the specific issue. I'm not particularly interested in the statutory commission, nor shall we deal with it. I'm interested only in the way these commissions were established, and I'll move right away to my specific question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So can you answer just briefly, yes or no, is a commission of expert established to prepare such a draft?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And then the Executive Board as the executive authority at local level reviews these documents and puts them before the Assembly as an official proposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The basic criterion for the election of the members of such a commission is their expertise and knowledge in an area, not their party affiliation. So it may easily happen that everyone on such a commission be without a party affiliations, not a member of any party?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Hypothetically speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Then you will agree with me that, following the same principle, this staff for regionalisation was formed, and I mean your specific example and the example of Mr. Stanisic and maybe one of the others about whom I can't be sure now. So this staff for regionalisation had nothing to do with party affiliations?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. I did not participate in the establishment of that staff or the election of particular personalities. But I think experts in -- in respective areas were elected to that staff primarily, not party leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And that is the main thrust of my question. I will not ask you further about how they met or how they worked. You explained that to the Prosecutor yesterday. We're done with this topic, and we're moving to the next one. You spoke about your own case, how you became an official in the Ilidza municipality. You're probably aware that there was, at the time, an inter-party agreement about the distribution of senior posts at every level between the three political parties.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I participated in the making of that inter-party agreement at the municipal level of Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, this is 1D113. It's called criteria for the distribution of municipal posts and departments endorsed by the representatives of the local parties: SDS, HDZ, and SDA; and it was signed by the leaders of these party, Alija Izetbegovic, Radovan Karadzic, and Stjepan Kljuic. Perhaps we can look at the first page on the screen to refresh your memory, 1D113.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember better now? Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see it, but I knew of its existence, and I know we put it into practice in Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And based on these criteria, you formed a government in the municipality of Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I see that my colleagues still do not have LiveNote, I have to pause and see if we can continue working before I resume my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I hear you, Mr. Cvijetic, but why can't we continue in the mean -- I understand they're working on it; it will be back shortly. But why can't we continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can, I can. I don't mind, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: However, Mr. Kezunovic, in order for one party to fill the vacancies, the posts that belong to it according to the electoral results and according to the agreed criteria, all the parties, including the Serbian Democratic Party, made an inventory of qualified staff within its own ranks, within its own membership, to see what kind of qualified personnel they disposed of to fill these posts. Do you know about this methodology?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I do. I was fully involved in the selection of personnel for senior posts in Ilidza municipality. And as president of the Executive Board, which means local prime minister, I was the one who proposed people to make up my own cabinet, so to speak. And I immediately faced one basic problem: That I did not have enough qualified, competent people for various sectors who had the proper education and training for specific activities. And that is why I proposed to keep some of the staff from the previous, let's say, Communist government because within my own party, I did not have such qualified staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You anticipated my next question. There's no need to rush. Let's just confirm, if you can, that these personnel lists, as we call them, although their full name is much longer, were made in this way. I'll show you the personnel list of the SDS for various posts, senior posts, in various municipal to republic bodies, and I'll show you that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 1D03-4116. 1D03-4116.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You can see, now, the title of the document.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It's a list of SDS members, potential candidates, for executive positions in the republican, town, and municipal organs of administration of funds and public companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask the usher to give you a hard copy. And if we could now turn to the next page on the screen, page 2. Next page, please, both in English and Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: As you can see, these potential candidates were grouped according to their area of expertise. This is the legal profession. And here you see the members of the SDS who are prominent experts in law. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: That's the end of the list of lawyers.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Expert in economics. You will see a list of prominent economists in Republika Srpska. Take a moment to look at the names.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And, finally, we come to your field of work. That's on to the next page. Engineering. This is the end of the list of economists.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we need page 6; science and engineering. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: On this list are also professionals in education and other areas; health care, et cetera. You've probably noticed that you are not on that list, and Mr. Stanisic is also not on the list, although he has a degree in law. Do you agree that it's precisely because you were not members of the SDS, because, on the first page of this document, we see a list of potential candidates from the SDS?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I suppose that's the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You know most of people from this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe this document is relevant, and I would like to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Why? Could you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, does this go to prove that Mr. Stanisic was not a member of the SDA -- SDS?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One of the main reasons is that. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: No, Mr. Cvijetic. This document is not relevant. It can't -- the absence of something can't prove the opposite.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is one of the corroborating pieces of evidence, and this witness is testifying precisely to these circumstances, namely, the membership of Mr. Stanisic in the Main Board and in other bodies of the Serbian Democratic Party. And I'm exploring various possibilities, and I'm not finding him on the list of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Cvijetic, what the Chamber has ruled is that it does not corroborate anything. By its nature, it cannot corroborate what you were seeking to so do. Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand your decision, Your Honours, and, of course, I accept it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kezunovic, my last question in this area is going to be direct. You knew Mr. Stanisic as minister of the interior and probably a member of the government. Let me ask you directly: Apart from his work in these capacities, did you ever notice his political engagement outside of his job? Before 1992, in 1992, and later.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that I do not really know Mr. Stanisic that well. Privately I met with him once, twice, or thrice, at various meetings, which were not limited to the two of us, and I did not notice any political engagement or political work by Mr. Stanisic within the SDS party or outside of it in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kezunovic, yesterday, while answering to the questions put to you by the Prosecutor, you confirmed that you were, for all practical purposes, the first person on the list of deputies of the SDS for the municipality of Ilidza, although you were not a member of the party. Let me now show you another document. It is 1D03-4137.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we didn't have time to obtain a translation of this document, since this is only a list, so names and surnames. We'll come to Ilidza list, where the witness will notice his name. And I will, in the meantime, explain what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So this document that has attached the collective lists, but the document itself is a reminder for voting. And, in the attachments, we have the collective lists for the voting for all the municipalities of the city of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have please have page 1 on the screen. And then, later on, we'll move to Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm, please, that it's stated here Centar Sarajevo, the collective list for the election of deputies into the Municipal Assembly of Sarajevo Centar, in this case?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have page 8, because that's where Ilidza is located. Bottom part of the page, please. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: This is where the lists for Ilidza start, but we haven't reached the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So can we please move to page 10, bottom part of the page, because at the bottom we will finds SDS. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kezunovic, it's easy to see that -- it is correct what you'd said, namely, that you are the first person in the list. Your name is under 1.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Radomir Kezunovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kezunovic, I can, again, provide you with this document in hard copy, if the usher would assist us, please. My question in relation to this document is the following: You can leaf through it just to see the situation in all the municipalities, and then I'll put my question to you. I gave the lists to Mr. Stanisic as well to review them. And you most probably know about Ilidza and maybe about some other municipalities. And what we've noticed was that it was not one party in not one municipality who put up on their lists people who were appointed -- who already held the positions of judges or public attorneys or lead policemen. So my question is: Do you know that people holding such positions could not even be candidates? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, I cannot confirm that that was part of the law at the time, but I think the rule was that people who were holding positions within state institutions could not be candidates. Nowadays, of course, it's very clear in the constitutional law of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It's stated like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So, in essence, they could not be involved in politics because they had to be or have to be independent; they should not be under political influence?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the essence of how it works.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, please pardon me if I'm confused. It seems to me that counsel is giving evidence. Could you frame a question --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll put a direct question then, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So you did agree with me that they cannot be members of political parties for the same reasons that we discussed?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, didn't the witness says that he doesn't know that for -- for this period? He knows it for now, but not for -- for then.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness did say. He said that it was not part of the electoral law, but it was applied in principle. That's what he said. I think that's we have in the transcript, but he can repeat that. MR. DI FAZIO: [Previous translation continues] ... he didn't say that. He didn't. He said that he can't confirm that it was part of the law, and he thinks that it was -- the rule. That's all he said. That's the highest you can put it at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And if I understand you well, Mr. Cvijetic, you -- you again try to prove with a list of names where some people are not in that they are not member of a political party or they couldn't be candidates because they had other jobs. But the -- the witness doesn't even know whether -- whether this list contains such persons or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we're now discussing the principle. The foundation for my question were the lists or specifically the list for Ilidza that the witness is already familiar with. He knows it by heart. But I can put my question directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Were the people who were at posts - in the prosecutor's office, police, or as judges - could they, at the time, be candidates for these positions?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can answer. I cannot confirm that according to the electoral law at the time it was strictly prohibited, but I can say for the municipality of Ilidza, where I was at a head of the list, that people who were in any way related to the army, police, or government structure be put on our list, list at Ilidza; they were not -- they could not be put on the list there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, may I ask, What is the direct purpose of this question? What exactly are you trying to prove, to obtain from the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have confirmed, until now, during our proceedings so far - and this witness can give his comments on this issue - that people who were at political functions or police functions at the time could not be candidates on such lists, and that was the essence of my question. We've received an answer from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... my question is, Who is this about?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are putting forward an argument that's opposite to the argument put forward by the Prosecution. They're saying that Mr. Stanisic was member of the SDS; we're saying that this shows he could not have been member of the SDS or any other political party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not only him, but also other members of the Ministry of Interior. MR. DI FAZIO: But this document can't go anywhere to proving that because all it's got is a list of names and ethnicity and place they come from. It doesn't have anything about who they are or what they do or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it wasn't my intention to tender this document. I showed it to the witness because I wanted to remind him of the list of the people who were candidates for the municipality of Ilidza. He confirmed and reminded himself about it. My intention was not to tender it. And the document's purpose was just to facilitate the witness's answer. I did receive an answer from him. May I continue, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kezunovic, my last question was prompted by your story about the flag that you removed from the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the building that we had seen photographed in the document we've just seen a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And in relation to your efforts to -- together with representatives of the Muslim population and the local structures, efforts to somehow avoid this or to make sure that the crisis would not develop. Now I will put my next question to you; namely, have you noticed any paramilitary organisation of members of the Muslim community in the municipality of Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In March 1992, and let me remind you that this was, at the time, following immediately several incidents in Bosnia, killing of a member of a wedding party, then the referendum on the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which took place on the 1st of March. In parallel with that, there were also preparations; we at Ilidza knew about those preparations for the Cutileiro Plan, which, objectively speaking, took into account all our analysis that we proposed for avoiding the conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina. However, part of all these incidents were -- were the appearance of this flag for instance. But also in the first half of March, on my way to work, when I came to the Assembly building, I found it filled with people who were in civilian clothes but were armed because under their coats one could see barrels. It was obvious that these people were armed. I didn't know who they were. There was about 20 of them. I didn't know who they were. And since the agreement existed and we discussed it between the police, security, and other organs representatives of the Bosniaks, what I did was I went to the first man of the municipality at the time, Mr. Mahmutovic, and I demand an explanation. What is this? What were these armed people doing in the Municipal Assembly building? What's their purpose? I wanted -- want immediately to explain that nobody stopped me while I was entering the building. It was only that I saw the armed people being there. I demanded the president to make sure that this would not happen again. Because, according to our expectations at the time, namely that Cutileiro Plan will finally revolve the situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina and that we -- Ilidza just must make sure to, for this period, to pass through without problems before the Cutileiro Plan starts functioning. So Mr. Tomo Kovac and Mr. Milijevic, Edin all worked on this together. But five or ten minutes after that, all these people were withdrawn. And that was the one incident that happened about an attempt of armed taking over of the municipality. But I was told that the Muslims had heard that Serbs were intending to take over the municipal building at the time, which, of course, was not true. And that's the incident I wanted to tell you about.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kezunovic. I have no further questions for you. This is the end of my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we don't have cross-examination for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Re-examination? MR. DI FAZIO: None, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Kezunovic, your testimony is at an end. We thank you for your attendance before the Tribunal. You are now released as a witness, and we wish you a safe journey back to your home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So I take it, Mr. Di Fazio, that that is it for the day? MR. DI FAZIO: I think that's the end of business for the day, if Your Honours please. I have no further applications or issues to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we take the adjournment, to resume in this courtroom at 9.00 tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 24th day of June, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 9.48 a.m.,
